summary: The primary meaning of QRY relates to collecting or gathering water, often in a basin or reservoir.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: قَرَى الضَّيْفَ is doubly trans.: see a verse cited voce قُوهٌ.

[meaning تَتَبَّعَ: see a verse of Aboo Dhu-eyb, voce خَافَةٌ, in art. خوف.] It also means He investigated a country or countries. (S, * K, * TA, all in art. قرى; and TA in art. قرو.) He made much and diligent search. (KL.) See also 10 in art. قرأ.
Entertainment for a guest; that with which a guest is entertained. (S.) Water collected in a trough, or tank, for the drinking of beasts: see بَيُّوتٌ: thus explained in the M in art. بيت.
A place where water runs, (T, S,) to, (T,) or in, or into, (S,) meadows, (T,) or a meadow. (S.) See شَيْخٌ (last sentence). Pl. أَقْرِيَةٌ: see قَرْءٌ.

A town, or village; (Msb, TA;) a small بَلَد, smaller than a مَدِينَة: (MF, voce تِرْمِ :) not well applied to a مَدِينَة unless qualified by an epithet denoting greatness. (TA in art. مَدِينَة.) See Bd, ii. 261.
نَاقَةٌ فِى قِرْوَتِهَا : see 4 in art. قرأ.
[vulg. قَرْيَة The yard of a ship; ] a squared piece of wood upon the head of the mast of a ship. (Az, TA in art. رنح.)
A certain bird. See خُضَارِىٌّ and تَنَوُّطٌ.
نَاقَةٌ قَرْوَاءُ A long-backed she-camel. (IB, in TA, voce هِرْجَابٌ.)
and مَقْرِىٌّ for مَقْرُوْءٌ: see art. قرأ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
